questions.q: Which of these is checked before a transaction can move from Incomplete to Complete?
options: Whether a valid customer with a bill-to site is present and at least one line has a valid amount
Whether the customer has ever been merged before
Whether the invoice has already been printed
Whether the customer has a bank account on file
questions.explain: Completion requires a valid customer/bill-to site, at least one valid line, resolvable accounting, and clean tax/freight calculation.

questions.q: What determines how strict the completion check is for a given transaction?
options: The customer's credit limit
The combination of transaction type and transaction source
The time of day the transaction was entered
The number of contacts on the customer account
questions.explain: As covered in lesson 12 and 13, transaction type and source together determine the level of control required before completion.

questions.q: Does printing or emailing a transaction change its accounting or balance status?
options: Yes, printing automatically closes the transaction
Yes, printing reverses the transaction
No — printing and emailing are distribution steps, separate from completion and accounting
Only batch printing affects the balance
questions.explain: Printing/emailing is purely about getting a copy to the customer; it has no effect on the transaction's accounting entries or open balance.

questions.q: What is the difference between on-demand and batch printing?
options: They are the same process with different names
On-demand is only for credit memos
Batch printing changes a transaction's transaction type
On-demand reprints a single transaction on request; batch runs on a schedule for everything completed since the last run
questions.explain: On-demand handles individual requests (like a customer calling for a copy); batch is the scheduled process most invoices go out through.

questions.q: In the Northwind Fixtures Co. example, why did the 397 AutoInvoice-imported invoices complete automatically overnight?
options: Because their source/type combination allowed automatic completion after passing AutoInvoice's validation
Because they were credit memos
Because they were all under the customer's credit limit
Because batch printing completes transactions automatically
questions.explain: A trusted, already-validated AutoInvoice source/type combination can be configured to complete transactions with less additional review.
